gloss: first calligraphy of the new year

definitions.gloss: first calligraphy of the new year
definitions.explanation: The practice of writing calligraphy for the first time in the new year, traditionally done on January 2nd. A longstanding Japanese New Year custom, often performed with a brush and ink.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{学校|がっこう}で{書|か}き{初|ぞ}めをした。
examples.english: The children did their first calligraphy of the year at school.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{書|か}き{初|ぞ}めは「{希望|きぼう}」という{字|じ}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: For this year's first calligraphy, I wrote the characters for 'hope.'

notes:
A traditional New Year custom, typically done on January 2nd ({一月二日|いちがつふつか}). People write auspicious words or phrases with brush and ink. Schools often assign {書|か}き{初|ぞ}め as a winter holiday task, and contests ({書|か}き{初|ぞ}め{大会|たいかい}) are held in January.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {書|か}き{初|ぞ}めをする: to do first calligraphy
- {書|か}き{初|ぞ}め{大会|たいかい}: calligraphy contest (New Year)
- {書|か}き{初|ぞ}め{展|てん}: calligraphy exhibition

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
The tradition dates back centuries. Writing on January 2nd ({仕事始|しごとはじ}め, the customary first work day) is considered to bring skill improvement throughout the year. Common words chosen include {希望|きぼう} (hope), {努力|どりょく} (effort), {平和|へいわ} (peace), and {新春|しんしゅん} (new spring).
